One intended response; at most three transient-failure attempts, first usable output retained, no quality/truncation regeneration; persistent attempt ledger, 600-second deadline and controlled backoff.
decisions.comments_or_revision: A usable captured response means non-whitespace report text attributable to the correct frozen task and retained with its raw response or stream evidence. It does not require all four sections, successful clinical interpretation or a normal finish reason. Preserve any recoverable partial text and do not discard it to obtain a replacement. A completed response with no report text is a terminal no-report outcome. Where no report text was captured, classify provider error codes and payloads before applying the HTTP retry list: authentication, unsupported parameters/models and permanent quota/billing errors stop the batch even if a response also has a generally retryable status code. Uncertain transient classification pauses for documented technical review rather than triggering an automatic content-selection opportunity.

decisions.proposed_decision: Review historical local candidate roster and proposed 8000-token budget; verify exact available identifiers and effective settings before freeze. No provider substitution or equal-compute claim.
decisions.comments_or_revision: Before formal generation, register each provider's exact model identifier or available snapshot, API route, reasoning/thinking configuration, output-token allowance and its documented semantics, timeout, SDK version and effective retry settings. Set reproducible request parameters explicitly where supported; where a setting is omitted, document the provider default and its verification date. Provider effort labels are not assumed to represent equal compute. Treat the existing 8,000 value as a historical candidate until a predeclared configuration check supports the intended evaluation. Use only synthetic material outside the selected 35 cases for any separately authorized live compatibility check; assess successful response capture, token-limit/finish behavior and parameter compatibility, not clinical answer quality or model ranking. Freeze all settings before formal case outputs, and do not change settings or regenerate reports in response to formal result quality.

flag_status_rule: Determine each semantic flag separately. A flag is positive once at least one confirmed in-scope issue satisfies its definition, even if another potentially qualifying issue remains pending. A flag is negative only after a complete issue review finds no confirmed or pending issue qualifying for that flag. Otherwise it is indeterminate. A pending issue relevant only to the other flag does not make this flag indeterminate once this flag has been fully assessed.
flag_clarifications: A control EMG route-C statement that all seven displayed max |z| values are below the supplied 3.65 endpoint is a displayed-value comparison and does not itself trigger the normality flag. A question presupposing an unsupported clinical deficit is assessed as an assertion under the existing rubric; the pathology flag for that presupposition requires a confirmed E02 issue, not question syntax alone. Other flag-qualifying assertions remain assessed under their applicable existing error categories. No new mandatory report content, error category or penalty is introduced.
